1Password Security Incident

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 1password

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Update: We will be providing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with details in the coming weeks once our full investigation is complete.
  • Recent findings suggest that on November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • The attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our owners.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update: We will be providing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with details in the coming weeks once our full investigation is complete.

Recent findings suggest that on November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

The attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our owners. These records include:.

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security).

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account).

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.

Recent findings suggest that other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers).

Industry observers note that the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning. During this incident there were a small number of customers in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them.

The keys that protect your vaults.

1Password does not store your account password or secret key.

1Password apps and browser extensions.

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added new detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

It has been revealed that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a newly introduced device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.

You trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

It has been revealed that we are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll revision it if we find anything that changes what we’ve mentioned here.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift.
  • According to recent reports, the Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem.
  • In a recent development, the Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift. Apple’s lineup includes the affordable Apple Watch SE 3 and the more advanced Apple Watch Series 12.

Here’s how those two Apple Watch models stack up….

According to recent reports, the Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem. It got a big patch last year, adding a variety of upcoming higher-end Apple Watch features. It now offers an Always-On display, sleep apnea notifications, temperature sensing, interactive wrist flick and double tap gestures, and more.

In a recent development, the Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode. It supports fast charging, going from 0-80% in 45 minutes.

Even though it hasn’t been updated in a year, the Apple Watch SE 3 is a very compelling option, especially for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem. It’s pretty fantastic that you can get an Apple Watch with key display and health-monitoring features for under $200.

Recent findings suggest that the Apple Watch Series 12 is Apple’s newest smartwatch, and it’s a significant revision over its predecessor. This year, Apple doubled down on the health and fitness capabilities of Apple Watch with an all-new Health Sensing System.

Apple touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 delivers “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” In fact, the organization conducted a study of more than 1,000 participants that found the Series 12 “achieved statistically better overall accuracy than every competing wearable it tested across workouts and daily activities.”.

With the upcoming system, Apple Watch Series 12 captures your heart rate every five seconds. Previous Apple Watch models, including the Apple Watch SE 3, take measurements every five minutes. The new Health Sensing System also enables a new readiness score feature, which factors in your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score.

Industry observers note that as I wrote in my review, the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some of the biggest improvements to Apple Watch health tracking in years. The upcoming sensing system unlocks a trove of new data along with better accuracy.

According to recent reports, the Apple Watch lineup is incredibly strong right now. Whether you’re deciding between the SE 3 and Series 12, both offer great health tracking, battery life, and connectivity. The Apple Watch SE 3 is an excellent choice for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem.

In a recent development, the Apple Watch Series 12, however, is the best Apple Watch for most people. There are major improvements to the health tracking capabilities, offering meaningful steps forward in what the Apple Watch can tell you about yourself. In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

What do you think of the current Apple Watch lineup? Are you shopping for one this holiday season? Let us know down in the comments.

Where buying individual pairs of dumbbells in five-pound increments up to 80 pounds would cost well over $1,500 (and take up a bunch of space in your home gym), adjustable dumbbells deliver the same versatility for a fraction of that price.

Pretty much every "best home dumbbells" list worth its salt will feature the PowerBlock Elite Adjustable Dumbbells near the top. In fact, I named them the most gift-worthy piece of home gym equipment in Lifehacker's first-ever "gift of the year" awards.

The weights have flat edges so you can hold them on end on your lap, and unlike a lot of adjustable models, they're compact enough that they won’t bump into each other on shoulder or chest presses.

These dumbbells also come in 70-pound and 90-pound versions. If you go with one of the smaller sets, you can also buy expansion sets later to upgrade to the larger versions. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that anthropic is launching a newly introduced tool for builders called Claude Ship. The new AI feature allows Claude to “review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows.”.

According to recent reports, claude Ship is a new product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

According to recent reports, “That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic claims. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals.

“Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually,” Anthropic claims.

“Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic says.

You can learn much more about Claude Ship here. Additional documentation can be found here.

Ariana Grande’s Best On-Screen Roles

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Now, she’s starring alongside Robert De Niro in the new movie Focker-In-Law, which is out this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ariana Grande may be one of the biggest pop stars in the world, but she’s also a true multi-hyphenate, known for her uncanny impressions and acting chops. Grande can hit a killer vocal run, produce a sleek beat, and steal a scene with terrific comedic timing. (It’s called range.) Her Hollywood career has grown with her pop star status — she started as a Broadway baby, singing her heart out in the musical 13, and eventually became one of Nickelodeon’s most beloved airheads as she played Cat Valentine on Victorious.

Now, she’s starring alongside Robert De Niro in the new movie Focker-In-Law, which is out this week. So what better time to look back at the roles that have helped the megastar get to this point? Here are some of her most impressive moments both on the big and small screens.

In a recent development, part of what makes Grande’s acting career so much fun to watch is that she never does what anyone is expecting her to do — and she’s not above extreme silliness. That makes her Zoolander 2 performance particularly entertaining. It’s extremely brief, but she pops on-screen just in time to have a wild orgy with Hansel (Owen Wilson). The scene marked her first time meeting Ben Stiller, who she reunites with in Focker-In-Law. She looked back at their meet-cute fondly during a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon: “He was directing me in an orgy scene in Zoolander 2 with a hippo and Susan Sarandon,” she shared. “So right off the bat, we had a comfortability.” —Julyssa Lopez.

Recent findings suggest that grande is one of the best parts of Adam McKay’s 2021 satire Don’t Look Up. She plays Riley Bina, a major pop star who is out-of-touch with the world — and the fact that a humanity-ending comet is headed Earth’s way. Once people start believing PhD student Kate Dibiasky (Jennifer Lawrence) and her advisor Dr. Randall Mindy (Leonardo DiCaprio) about their chilling prediction, Bina performs her latest song “Just Look Up” with her cheating boyfriend, DJ Chello (Kid Cudi). The scene finds Grande delivering killer one-liners like, “Listen to the goddamn qualified scientists, we really fucked it up this time” while suspended onstage and sporting a ridiculous get-up of white feathers. According to McKay, many of the song’s lyrics were improvised by Grande. —Maya Georgi.

In 2013, Nickelodeon adapted Gordon Korman’s 2008 novel Swindle, shaping it into a made-for-television heist movie revolving around two friends who set out to recover a $1.2 million baseball card. They form an unlikely group with other kids from their school harboring secret skills, and Grande steps in as a cheerleader with an undercover geeky side. The film came during her Sam & Cat days, and teamed her up with co-star Jennette McCurdy, while also letting her go beyond her flaky Cat persona. —J.L.

In a recent development, when Grande reprises the role of Glinda for the second half of the Wicked tale, she’s planning her wedding to Prince Fiyero, all of Emerald City idolizes her, and everything is as she always wished — or is it? As Glinda reevaluates her life and decides to change paths to help her friend Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo), there are fewer of the rollicking comedy moments that made Grande’s performance in the first film so fun to watch. But with major songs like “I Couldn’t Be Happier,” “The Girl in the Bubble,” and the booming duet “For Good,” she makes clear why she was a natural fit for the iconic role. —Kate Storey.

It has been revealed that guest-starring on the campy horror-comedy television show Scream Queens as Chanel #2 was Ariana Grande’s first adult role after leaving Nickelodeon’s Sam & Cat to focus on her music. Creator Ryan Murphy said in 2015 that initially, Grande “was just going to do one episode, but she loved the process so much that she wanted to do more.” Even though she played a corpse in a few of those episodes, Ari’s comedic skills shine through, especially in a scene where her character’s ghost visits Emma Roberts’ Chanel #1. Grande is hilarious when speaking about her afterlife in hell. Whether her character is that she’s in a bad mood because Adolf Hitler was motorboating her boobs or that Jesus broke into heaven and stole the dinosaurs, she steals every scene. —Alison Weinflash.

Let’s look beyond the fact that Cat Valentine seemingly has a legitimate lobotomy in the middle of the Victorious run. There would not be an Ariana Grande without the exposure, preparation, and genuine war stories that the cast ofVictorious went through. While the will-they-won’t-they nature of Cat’s relationship with Robbie (Matt Bennett) was finally resolved in the apocalyptic music video for “One Last Time,” the most memorable musical moments of the series all involved Grande: from the karaoke bar rendition of “Give it Up” to the “They didn’t say I couldn’t sing” riff on the Victorious iCarly collab “Leave It All to Shine.” As Cat, Grande earned her place in the Hollywood Arts High School hall of fame and started her path toward becoming a household name. —C.T. Jones.

Ariana Grande has hosted SNL three times now, and she always makes her appearances memorable by leveraging her exceptional impersonation skills, showcasing her comedy agility, and refusing to shy away from being wildly silly. We’ve seen her play Jennifer Lawrence during a Family Feud recreation and playing a shy intern who saves her radio station with her ability to sound like everyone from Shakira to Celine Dion. But her most beloved contributions might be in an off-key bridesmaid in the famed Domingo skit and giving us a hilarious take on Home Alone. —J.L.

Grande’s character in Focker In Law, Olivia Jones, is a multi-hyphenate not unlike the actress who portrays her. Just swap the gold records for FBI credentials, throw in vegan cooking chops, and you have a future in-law (to grandpa Jack Byrnes, reprised brilliantly by Robert De Niro) hell-bent on entering the “circle of trust” in record time. Grande plays the ultra-competitive Liv with exacting comedic timing, offering the perfect foil for Ben Stiller’s goofball insecurity. —Shirley Halperin.

It takes self-determination, drive, and a lot of pink to make the world’s most coveted role your own. Ariana Grande wasn’t the frontrunner when Universal first announced it would be making a Wicked film. But the Petal singer fought to claim Glinda’s glitter wand. “Oz has been my safe space for as long as I can remember,” she wrote in an open letter to fans before the film’s premiere. It’s hard to imagine a world where the gleeful shrieks of Grande’s “Popular” outro didn’t exist — and her participation in the John M. Chu duology is a career-defining moment, proof the former Nick star is never far from her musical theater roots. —C.T.J.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Offering support for iPhone and Android’s tracking networks, the newly introduced Kodak SlideTag offers the neat added functionality over an AirTag of being able to show your photos and more on an E-Ink display.

The Kodak SlideTag is inspired by classic 35mm slides from Kodak cameras, and is built by the same organization, Reto, that launched a keychain digital camera inspired by old Kodak cameras too. The tracker’s E-Ink display is designed mainly to showcase your photos, with storage built-in for up to 12 photos, but also the ability to show lists and QR codes.

The SlideTag’s extra features are controlled by the Kodak Memory Link app, while tracking is handled in the Find My app on iPhone just like an AirTag (and the Find Hub app on Android phones).

There are nine total styles for the SlideTag, all sold in a blind box format. You can order one tracker for $35 with the whole set also available for purchase.

Eight of the styles have a one-in-eight chance of finding, while the ninth style is only found in one out of every 64 boxes.

Kodak SlideTag is available today from Amazon.

Wu-Tang Clan showcased a slew of classic hits during the NFL Thanksgiving Day Game Halftime Show.

The annual match-up pitted the Chicago Bears against the Detroit Lions at at Ford Field in Detroit, with the hip-hop group taking the field midway through. The game, which aired on CBS, also saw Broadway singer Antonio Cipriano performing the National Anthem.

The group, joined by Red Hot Chili Peppers’ Chad Smith on drums, kicked it off with “Triumph” from their 1997 album Wu-Tang Forever. The rappers also showcased a medley that included “C.R.E.A.M,” “Da Mystery of Chessboxin,” and “Bring Da Ruckus.” Notably, Ol’ Dirty Bastard’s son Young Dirty Bastard performed his father’s lines off 1995 single “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.”.

Sources indicate that wu-Tang Clan played a small (but apocryphally pivotal) role in the team’s championship run. During Game Four, the Wu-Tang Clan provided the halftime entertainment, taking the stage when the Knicks were down a seemingly insurmountable 29 points. If you're on the lookout for a good deal on a portable projector, I recommend considering the following XGIMI deals.

If you're looking for the most affordable option, the Vibe One projector is just $179 (originally $299) after a 40% discount. This is a 1080p resolution and 1500:1 contrast portable projector for casual watching at night with 250 ISO lumens of brightness, and the price reflects that. It already comes with Google TV, which is my favorite OS, so you can download and stream any app you want. It's battery-powered, which means you can take it anywhere with you (as long as you have wifi). The battery life more than doubles to two and a half hours in Eco Mode, while still keeping the projector under three pounds. It also has Google TV as its OS, but the projection is 360° with its adjustable built-in stand. You also have the option of getting the bundle with the PowerBase Stand, which extends the battery to five hours. Like the Vibe One, it has a built-in speaker, but this one uses dual 6W Harman Kardon speakers with Dolby Audio.The MoGo 4 Laser is a slightly upgraded version that uses triple laser technology for a better picture. It still supports 1080p resolution, but it's brighter with 550 ISO lumens and a 1000:1 contrast. The battery life, OS system, stand, speakers, and auto keystone technology are the same—but the bundles are different, so they're worth considering if they fit your needs.

It supports 4K resolution, uses RGB triple laser brightness that reaches 4800 ISO lumens (bright enough to see during the day), has a 120Hz refresh rate and gaming features to make gaming smooth, displays an 8,000:1 native contrast to make colors and blacks pop, and supports IMAX Enhanced, Dolby Vision, and HDR10+. The auto keystone is just as powerful as the other options, but the lens adds an optical zoom and a Lens Memory feature, which lets you save up to six custom lens and image setups and recall them with a click. Right now, it's down to $1,899 (originally $2,499) after a 24% discount.

The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with new customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube revision.

Recent findings suggest that in the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app rolled out on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

Industry observers note that android Authority spotted several new app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta upgrade (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow users to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

That said, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

We've tested the best smartwatches, and these are the 3 I recommend for iPhone and Android

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The best smartwatch is almost always the one that works with your phone.
  • Industry observers note that one of the remaining holdouts is Amazfit, which released the excellent Active 3 Premium that works on iPhone and Android.
  • It's incredible value, but if you're looking for the closest integration you can get with your phone or smart features like emergency or health alerts, then I'd recommend the Apple Watch Series 12 (iPhone) or Google Pixel Watch 5 (Android) right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The best smartwatch is almost always the one that works with your phone. Over the past few years, brands have moved away from universal compatibility and toward platform-specific watches that will only work if you use a particular phone.

Industry observers note that one of the remaining holdouts is Amazfit, which released the excellent Active 3 Premium that works on iPhone and Android. It's half the price of Apple or Google's watches, but you wouldn't know it from its impressive fitness tracking features.

It's incredible value, but if you're looking for the closest integration you can get with your phone or smart features like emergency or health alerts, then I'd recommend the Apple Watch Series 12 (iPhone) or Google Pixel Watch 5 (Android) right now.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The Amazfit Active 3 Premium is the smartwatch I recommend for most people, and not just because it works with whichever phone you have. It's a fantastic fitness-tracking watch that easily holds its own against the Apple Watch Series 12 and Google Pixel Watch 5, without locking you to a specific platform or phone.

Recent findings suggest that it is also incredible value — coming in at around half the price of the two flagship watches — and all the features are free with no subscription (unless you need Zepp Aura, the sleep-focused AI wellness app that generates audio to relax you). It has offline maps, tracks more than 170 activities, and comes with built-in GPS.

It has a smaller footprint (wristprint?) than many other smartwatches, with a 1.3-inch display, compared to the 1.77- or 1.96-inch Apple Watch Series 12. It's not a huge amount on paper, but it makes a big difference, as it felt smaller and less noticeable on our wrist. It's a shame it doesn't come in a few more vibrant colors, though.

While you don't get the smarts of Apple and Google's watches (emergency alerts, on-watch calls, third-party apps), fitness and activity tracking is where the Active 3 Premium really shines, with metrics to rival the best Garmin watches, like heart rate, blood oxygen, stress levels, cycle tracking, sleep quality and skin temperature.

In a recent development, the data all syncs to your phone, and you can view it and get insights in the Zepp app, available for Android and iPhone. If you ever used a Fitbit before the Google takeover, the Zepp app is the closest thing to that now-gone experience; easy to understand, straightforward to use, and guides you through all the different metrics.

This is particularly helpful if you're just getting into running, as the running features on the Active 3 Premium are almost as detailed as those you'd find on Garmin watches, yet everything is explained clearly, even for more complex topics like your lactate threshold and ground contact time, which assess how your foot strikes the floor.

Amazfit claims that the Active 3 Premium should last 12 days between charges. Like most other smartwatches, that doesn't work out in the real world; we found that it'd generally last just over a week or eight days. That's down a bit on the spec, but still miles ahead of the 24-hour battery life on the Apple Watch Series 12.

It has been revealed that apple, Google and Samsung refresh their watches every year. Normally, these are pretty small upgrades, so I often recommend buying the previous year's model. But not with the Apple Watch Series 12. For the first time in almost half a decade, Apple has given the watch a pretty major health-tracking update.

Industry observers note that the most significant change is that there's a new, more accurate heart rate sensor. This powers a few other changes, like the Readiness score you can get each day. This is something imported from other running watches and is a measure of how you've recovered after activity and how to improve the score.

I've tested watches with this kind of score and haven't found it that informative, but I know our resident runners find it particularly helpful when training for races. The improved sensors also allow for continuous heart rate monitoring (ie all day), which was previously limited to just during tracked workouts.

Sources indicate that these practical and useful changes were only part of the Series 12 pitch. Apple also rolled out upcoming AI Siri and a selection of 'helpful' AI-powered features, called Audio Intelligence. There are two (Live Rewind, Siri Recap), but both use the watch to capture speech around you and turn it into some form of recap.

Live Rewind is arguably the least helpful and most invasive. It listens to conversations (privately on your phone) and allows you to rewind live conversations in case you miss a detail, like someone's name (in case you were unaware you could ask the person to repeat what they said). Recap uses AI to summarize all that data into a journal-like, 'here's what happened today' note.

Industry observers note that honestly, these seem like gimmicks to me that very few people will ever use, and it normalizes surveillance. So, in case it wasn't clear, I wouldn't buy the watch for these and would jump into the settings to disable them. But in all other aspects, the Series 12 is the best Apple Watch you can buy right now and a worthy upgrade.

As with the Apple Watch, I wouldn't normally recommend the most recent version of the Google Pixel Watch, but this time I do think the Google Pixel Watch 5 is the better choice than the 4, but mostly because it's hard to find a fresh edition of the Pixel Watch 4 now that the Pixel Watch 5 exists.

That doesn't mean I don't think the Pixel Watch 5 is a great smartwatch — it is — but it's a relatively modest enhancement this time around. But what you get for your money still makes it the best smartwatch for Android phones, especially if you own a Pixel device. And like Apple, it's the fresh health and safety features that are the headline.

The Pixel Watch 5 includes Breathing Emergency Detection, which is a lot like 2024's Loss of Pulse Detection, which uses the watch's sensor data to look for signs of a breathing emergency and automatically requests 911 support or trusted contacts for help. These two, along with Fall/Crash Detection, Blood Pressure Trends, and Insulin Resistance Trends, form part of Google's latest "Health Guardian" suite.

Technologically, it's impressive. But do I recommend you buy the watch for them? I don't think so. It's a reassuring fallback if you do have an emergency, but you can't say with certainty that they'll always work as intended when you need them to. And reviewers (including us) can't really test them to check either.

Industry observers note that what I like about the Pixel Watch range is that Google doesn't tie too many features exclusively to Pixel phones. The Pixel-exclusive features on the Watch 5 are: call screening, secure phone unlock, contact cards when someone calls you, and the ability to use your watch as a remote viewfinder for your phone's camera app.

According to recent reports, the newest watch has also retained my favorite feature: repairable screens and replaceable batteries. This isn't as easy as popping the back off, but it makes the Pixel Watch 5 the most repairable smartwatch you can buy right now. iFixit even rated it a near-perfect 9/10 for repairability, while the Apple Watch Series 12 scored just 4/10.

In a recent development, it's not easy for me to praise Google (have you seen the Google Graveyard?), but it's a hugely positive move that saves you money in the long run and prevents otherwise good watches from going to the trash. But much of this was also true of the Pixel Watch 4, so if you can find a good deal on the older model, I'd go for that.

Industry observers note that if you're after the best smartwatch for your phone, the three models I recommend above are going to cover most use cases, whichever phone you have. But there are a lot more smartwatches around right now.

According to recent reports, not every model can be the best, but some come pretty close. If you need a few more options, these are the smartwatches I still think are worth your money, and may fill a need we didn't cover in the wearables from Amazfit, Apple or Google.

Industry observers note that last year's Apple Watch Series 11 is so close to the older Series 10 that it does make you wonder why Apple released it, but for the first time in many years, there was a bump in battery life from 18 hours on the Series 10 to 24 hours on the Series 11. If you can get a good discount, it's a great option, but the Series 12 is a much better watch for not much more.

Read our full Apple Watch Series 11 review.

In a recent development, the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 generates free wellbeing insights from your data. This is a neat upside, as many other brands charge for this. The (potential) downside is that you need a Samsung phone to access them all in the Samsung Health app. But it's more expensive than the Galaxy Watch 8, despite modest changes and the same display. The Pixel Watch 5 is a better option unless you really need the Samsung integration.

Read our full Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 review.

Sources indicate that apple didn't release a fresh budget watch in 2026, so the most recent is the 2025 SE 3. It's an excellent choice and has almost all the same features as the Series 10 and 11, minus some health-specific ones like ECG and blood oxygen monitoring. And like those models, it lacks the upgraded health sensors of the Series 12. If you can do without them, the SE 3 is a great value Apple Watch.

Read our full Apple Watch SE 3 review.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is a useful upgrade from the Ultra 3 with a redesigned, more accurate health sensor array and better battery life. It also comes with the same AI gimmicks as the Series 12. It's a good option if you need a larger, longer-lasting Apple Watch, but for most people, the Series 12 is the better (and cheaper) choice.

Read our full Apple Ultra 4 review.

The Withings ScanWatch Light is a stripped-back version of the hybrid ScanWatch 2 I wear every day. It doesn't have a large color screen and is missing features like calls and apps, but it can track your activity, heart rate and workouts. I love the ScanWatch 2, and the compromise to reduce the cost is that the Light drops the flagship watch's health features, like an ECG. Otherwise, this is an excellent fitness tracking watch that'll last several weeks between charges.

Read our full Withings ScanWatch Light review.

The CMF Watch 3 Pro is impressively cheap, retailing for less than most fitness trackers. It has a color display and two weeks of battery life; incredible at this price. But we found that step counts are inaccurate and the sleep tracking is unreliable. So I'd recommend the Amazfit Active 3 Premium instead.

Read our full Nothing CMF Watch 3 Pro review.

Industry observers note that we reviewed the first Apple Watch more than a decade ago, and we've been testing the best smartwatches ever since. The devices have gotten more complex, last longer and have way more features now, but the core of our testing has remained the same: we wear the watches, just as you would, to see how they hold up in the real world.

Industry observers note that we look at how easy it is to set up, whether it has compatibility issues with specific phones and spending hours poking around in the software, looking for settings, apps and other features that make the device worth your money. Over the years, these watches have transitioned from phone companions to health and wellbeing trackers.

So we also focus on how these tools work, whether the tracking is accurate, how it compares to the competition and whether there's value in measuring what the firm says you should. We wear the best smartwatches out on runs, during workouts, while sleeping and going about our day to see how they cope.

Over the past few years, brands have added more safety features to their watches, like irregular heartbeat notifications, sleep apnea alerts, crash and fall detection and hypertension alerts. These are things we can't practically test, so we can't verify that these work as intended or described.

Industry observers note that in the U.S., health features are regulated by the FDA, so there is some degree of verification, but because we can't check that ourselves, I wouldn't recommend that you buy any of these watches specifically for these safety features. At the very least, they should be secondary to some other safety check.

It's not something you can predict, but sometimes a health problem does come along when you're testing a smartwatch. This happened to one of our writers — her Garmin watch alerted her to a potential heart problem she didn't know about, and that prompted her to go to the hospital to get checked out.

Recent findings suggest that before you go too far into your journey for a newly introduced smartwatch, first you need to work out which ones will work with your phone. The Apple Watch only works with iPhones, and some Android-focused watches have features that are exclusive to specific phones (I'm thinking of offerings from Google and Samsung here).

There are plenty of options that'll work with both platforms, but they generally aren't the flagship models that get a lot of attention every summer and fall, like the watch I rate as the best smartwatch right now, the Amazfit Active 3 Premium. It's more of a fitness smartwatch, but it can do a lot of what the others can do for a lot less.

And that's one of the other big choices you have to make: do you want a fitness watch that has smartwatch features, or a smartwatch as a companion to your phone that can track your fitness? These sound similar — and they are — but the difference is how much of the focus is put on either the smartwatch or fitness features.

Sources indicate that fitness smartwatches evolved from the best fitness trackers, with larger displays and more sensors. The best smartwatches started life as Bluetooth-connected extensions of your phone and over time became devices that keep you connected to your digital life, even when you're away from your phone working out.

Sources indicate that the Apple Watch Series 12 and Google Pixel Watch 5 are the best compromise between the two, but there are plenty of other options in our Also Consider section that also straddle that line or lean one way or the other. Though, if you need a cellular connection in your watch, those are pretty much limited to the flagship models.

Robot vacuums have been around a while, but it can still be tough to find one that is also good at mopping. But unlike many robot vacuum and mop combos that use spinning pads, the all-in-one Eufy E25 robot vacuum and mop has a self-cleaning roller mop: The roller is rinsed with clean water as it mops, then cleaned at the dock, meaning you don't need to spend as much time cleaning it yourself. It's a smart design, and it's a great time to pick one up: Right now, the E25 is 43% off for Black Friday, taking it down to $569.96 (originally $999.99).

Another perk is that the E25 is equipped with an anti-tangle brush and multiple side brushes that get into tight corners; this is a valuable feature at this price point, as is the 20,000 Pa suction power, which results in a deeper clean on both hard flooring and carpeting, features that are especially appealing for pet owners.

According to recent reports, owners can map an area, set zones, schedule cleans, and define different features via the Eufy Clean app; the customizable options include cleaning intensity, suction power, water level, and deciding whether you want the E25 to make multiple passes in an area. It uses LiDAR mapping and AI for obstacle detection and is highly automated, with a dock that empties the robot, washes and dries the roller mop, and refills its water supply. If you live in a home with pets and want a low-maintenance robot vacuum and mop that can handle routine floor cleaning with minimal intervention, the Eufy E25 can cut some serious time from your cleaning routine.

According to recent reports, openAI is bringing GPT-6.2 Sol to the Chat tab in ChatGPT today, less than a week after the model debuted in Work and Codex. The tech giant also set a retirement date for two older models.

OpenAI indicates it tuned this version of Sol for everyday conversation. It’s better at picking out details in photos, like the symbols on a parking sign, and following your instructions when searching the web.

It has been revealed that if you’re comparing hotels for a weekend trip, for example, ChatGPT can weigh a shorter walk against a lower nightly rate. It can also offer to alert you when something you’re shopping for drops in price.

The global rollout starts today for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.

As for the outgoing models, OpenAI notes it will retire GPT-5.6 Sol from Chat, Work, and Codex on December 23.

GPT-5.6 Terra will also leave ChatGPT Work and Codex on the same day next month.

‘Hejira’ at 50: Beck, Cameron Crowe, Clairo, and More Honor Joni Mitchell’s 1976 Masterpiece

💡 Key Takeaways
  • J oni Mitchell wanted to go ice skating.
  • Mitchell had recently cancelled the remainder of her Hissing of Summer Lawns tour, performing her last show at the nearby Dane County Memorial Coliseum.
  • Legendary photographer Joel Bernstein captured this moment, which would eventually appear inside the gatefold for her next album: Hejira.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

J oni Mitchell wanted to go ice skating. It was February 1976, and she was standing on the edge of a frozen Lake Mendota in Madison, Wisconsin, wearing a black ermine cape and a black wool hat. All she needed were black skates to match. “I had a hell of a time getting the guy to give me black skates,” she recalled to Cameron Crowe, decades later. “He remarked, ‘Black skates are for, for men, madam.’ I said, ’No, no, you don’t understand. I’m having a funeral for my dead tour. I need black.”.

Mitchell had recently cancelled the remainder of her Hissing of Summer Lawns tour, performing her last show at the nearby Dane County Memorial Coliseum. She was exhausted, battling a cocaine addiction, and reeling from the breakup with her drummer John Guerin, which she’d later describe as “one of the most special relationships” she’d ever had. This was her wake for it all, a farewell ride through the ice — not so different from the “River” she dreamt about skating on just five years prior. The ice was starting to thaw, and there were loud crashing sounds coming from the nearby trees, a sound she likened to “cases of Coca-Cola smashing.” She began to skate anyway, her black outfit standing in stark contrast to the backdrop.

Legendary photographer Joel Bernstein captured this moment, which would eventually appear inside the gatefold for her next album: Hejira. On the front cover, taken by Norman Seef, she’s wearing a black beret and holding a cigarette, stoically staring at the camera (she wanted it to look like an Ingmar Bergman film, she said), as a wide, open road is juxtaposed below. The artwork indicated the mission statement of Hejira — in the same way she skated away on that ice and didn’t look back, Mitchell got in her car and drove. “The Hejira album was written mostly while I was traveling in the car,” she told Crowe, in her 1979 Rolling Stone cover story. “That’s why there were no piano songs, if you remember. Hejira was an obscure word, but it said exactly what I wanted. Running away, honorably.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Sources indicate that mitchell took three journeys while making Hejira: a portion of Bob Dylan’s all-star Rolling Thunder Revue Tour in late 1975, her short-lived Hissing trek in early 1976, and a cross-country drive she made in a white Mercedes without a license (she’d often wear a red wig in disguise, and go by names like Charlene Latimer and Joan Black). Released in November 1976, the album is a timeless travelogue of jazz-folk magic, when Mitchell left it all behind in search for more. “I’m porous with travel fever,” she sings on the aching title track. “But you know I’m so glad to be on my own.”.

In a recent development, it’s impossible to pinpoint the genius of Hejira on just one track. There’s the opener “Coyote,” about the affair she had with the playwright Sam Shephard on the Rolling Thunder tour. That song is now immortalized in a viral video from Martin Scorsese’s documentary, where she casually performs it for a stunned Dylan, Roger McGuinn, and Gordon Lightfoot. There’s “Furry Sings the Blues,” about her encounter with the Memphis blues legend who didn’t exactly take a liking to her (yes, that’s her longtime pal Neil Young on the harmonica). The stunning “Amelia,” named after Amelia Earhart, was her ode “from one solo pilot to another …sort of reflecting on the cost of being a woman and having something you must do.” Hejira is arguably her most cohesive body of work, featuring the fretless bass of Jaco Pastorius — whom she called the bass player of her dreams — plus guitarist Larry Carlton, percussionist Bobbye Hall, and others.

Looking back, Mitchell knew she was at the height of her powers. “I feel a lot of people could have written ’Chelsea Morning,’” she said. “But I don’t think anyone else could have written the songs on Hejira.” In honor of the 50th anniversary of Hejira, Rolling Stone spoke with musicians and actors about its legacy, and why it continues to resonate with listeners today. And in a full-circle moment, Crowe, who is right now working on a Mitchell biopic, pays tribute to the record he discussed with Mitchell in this very magazine, all those years ago. According to recent reports, I’ve been a Joni Mitchell fan for a really long time, since I was a kid. And one of my best friends who passed away, we were obsessed with her. She was the one who actually introduced me to Joni Mitchell through Blue, because we would just listen to the album all the time. So through a general obsession with her, I just eventually went through all of her albums. And I really remember being particularly attached to Hejira when I was a teenager. I would go on long walks around my neighborhood [in Oak Park in Illinois], listening to that album, and just be really emotional.

It has been revealed that jaco’s bass literally captures the feeling of being on a trip and moving. He uses his bass as a vehicle on that album in such a cool way. And Joni’s lyrics feel like being on a road trip, listening to somebody’s stories. It reminds me of being with my parents, driving. We always drive from Chicago to Georgia where my family’s from, and just being on the road and talking.

Recent findings suggest that the album itself feels like a departure. She’s going on a journey and choosing to go away from the industry for a minute, and that is captured sonically in a really interesting way. With Hejira, she distills the feeling of loneliness in a way that she hadn’t done before. Each song is dealing with loneliness, but she puts it into these different scenarios and narratives. They all come together to tell this one story of being a woman who’s alone, just traveling.

In Martin Scorsese’s film The Rolling Thunder Review: A Bob Dylan Story, there is a moment where Joni plays her latest song, “Coyote,” at Gordon Lightfoot’s house. I love that there is footage of the early creation of this song. The lyrics change a little on the album, but you can see in her eyes the memories are very powerful as she sings and remembers. She had just written “Coyote” on a bus when she was with the tour, as she looked out at the “white lines on the freeway,” after she had a brief, tumultuous affair with the playwright Sam Shepard. Most of us have had these youthful, quick assignations, and I love being in her head as she reconciles the moment through her poetry and lyricism. Hejira is filled with emotion and hunger and as a young woman. Hejira helped me with the complexities of life, love, and longing.

It’s something that stayed with me my whole life. Being somebody who makes records and always having trouble listening to records because you’re just always thinking about technically how they were made, it’s a beautiful example of just being so disconnected from any kind of process. It doesn’t bear examination. I just find it 100 percent an emotional reactive experience. It conjures up something that I am so desperate to hold onto in my life. Basically what I’m saying is, I’m just a sad, pathetic fan, really.

Those things get chipped away gradually, as you meet all your heroes and make a lot of music. You never really listen to music the same way. But I’m a teenager again when I listen to it. I don’t know if it’s the imagery or the fact that she has this incredible way of weaving a narrative that is just so difficult to do in song. I mean, poetry is powerful, but the combination of melody and poetry is this kind of witchcraft that has always cast a spell on me.

Sources indicate that she’s my favorite artist. And this record is an apex of confidence. She’s really just doing what she wants, to the nth degree. She’s this crazy sort of enigmatic, weird figure. You hear all these stories about her. She’s a manifestation of something that is so rare and special that my version of her that I have in my heart and my idea of who she is, I’m just clinging onto it for dear life. It’s like a hero I never want to meet. She could be the nicest, warmest person on Earth, but she wouldn’t be this person that she’s created in my mind personally, by my personal relationship with her music.

I remember hearing a long time ago that Joni wrote most of Hejira while she was on a road trip across America, and ever since then, I’ve always listened to it on long drives. It just makes so much sense to me. The whole record feels like it’s constantly moving, whether you’re speeding down a highway or sitting in traffic watching the sun go down.

Recent findings suggest that as a drummer first, I’m always listening for the drums and percussion on records. To me, they’re kind of the heartbeat of any modern album. I know a lot of Joni’s records don’t have much drumming on them, but the fact that Hejira is constantly chugging along without a lot of full kit drumming continues to blow my mind. And I think Jaco’s bass playing adds this whole other rhythmic dimension to her music.

In a recent development, I’ve always thought of Joni as a percussionist in her own way. The way she attacks the guitar strings, the rhythms she creates with her strumming, it’s unlike anything I’ve ever heard from another musician. It’s one of the most fascinating things about her playing to me. And then you have Jaco on bass, another absolute master of rhythm, and the two of them create this incredible, almost hypnotic pulse that runs through the whole record.

And Bobbye Hall’s percussion adds so much to that feeling. It’s never overpowering, but there’s so much movement and texture in what she’s doing. All these little rhythmic details that somehow make the music feel even more alive. Between the three of them, there’s this constant sense of motion, like the music is always pushing forward but never in a hurry to get anywhere.

In a recent development, hejira was the Joni album that helped me meet Joni. I feel like her truest self comes through on this record so beautifully, and it’s an anchor on tour when the roads are never ending and the bus forever rumbling. My favorite song is “Coyote.”.

Recent findings suggest that hejira is Joni’s culmination to my mind. Her greatest songs, the greatest band, the greatest recordings, the most revelatory. The signature Roland Jazz Chorus guitar amp tone. Jaco Pastorius truly unleashed. The concepts and material mined into their seventh and eighth minute in some cases. I like to believe her whole catalog was leading to this moment. She’s at the height of her powers, and the masterworks that follow (Don Juan’s Reckless Daughter, Mingus, Night Ride Home, Turbulent Indigo, etc.) feel possible because of what Hejira unlocked. The writing is perhaps the most challenging, but the experience remains incredibly propulsive; you’re carried along by bearing witness to a human truly unrestrained by self-doubt, by adhering to any kind of rules or any kind of culture, someone in the midst of their quest to express their purest self. Maybe that sounds vague, but anyone that knows the record knows exactly what I’m talking about. When I’ve been asked about it, I’ve jokingly replied, “It’s as far as music has come.” But maybe that’s actually true.

I was touring extensively through my twenties, and I think it was at least 10 months of the year I was just on the road constantly. It was such a grind, but music had become a companion. We all had our headphones, and you’d sit on these long plane rides and bus rides listening to records. So it’s a lot of time to take a lot of deep dives. The whole Odelay tour, I was listening to Joni on the bus. It was pretty much Joni, Françoise Hardy records from the mid Sixties, and Morricone soundtracks — but not the Westerns, the weirder stuff. And then I had a CD of a rainstorm in Hawaii. That was all I listened to. It was like Joni and a Hawaiian rainstorm.

Hejira is the sound of an artist who has evolved so deeply into their own voice and their own craft. It’s a thing to behold. It’s a place that not a lot of artists even get to. Either they’re not really on that search to cultivate that rarefied place in their work, or they’re distracted by success and fame and touring, which happens to anybody who gets caught up in the sort of mechanics of the music business. So I think it’s even more of a singular achievement that she was able to make this after being on such a nonstop, relentless decade of making albums and touring. Usually at that point, somebody would just want to disappear for five years.

Recent findings suggest that the music doesn’t necessarily sound like anything she had done before. One thing that’s really striking to me is the guitar sound. The effect on her guitar is a chorus pedal. The first one came out the year she was making the record. This was brand new technology. So this is like, “This new weird thing came out, and I’m going to put it on my entire album.” Not even, “Let’s vet this and see if this is cool. Is this going to be trendy? Is this going to sound dated?” This chorus pedal becomes the sound of whole genres afterwards. I don’t think it really becomes part of the palette of popular music till maybe the early 2010s. You listen to almost all of indie rock, from Mac DeMarco, to pop artists.

And then you also get the guitar sound of Prince’s Purple Rain, which comes from this record, without a doubt. It is interesting that something that is uncompromising, and not even her most popular album or most iconic, still managed to have an imprint on pop. Honestly, I think the sound of this even filters into shoegaze and Cocteau Twins. I don’t know if people have put those things together, but I see it clearly.

Sources indicate that she is so mature as an artist on this record. I mean, it would take you more than a lifetime to get to that maturity. Somehow, she did it.

I first listened to Hejira in full on a tour bus driving through Europe. Highway rushing past, barren fields and long stretches of countryside out the window, the way Joni intended (I think). It struck me immediately as a timeless record. None of the songs are shorter than four minutes, the longest one being almost nine, but somehow they all feel intentional. She doesn’t waste words. I was so intrigued by that concept, of letting the story speak for itself, and setting up a bed of guitars that could support it. It inspired my writing a lot during that time, specifically a song I wrote while on that tour called “Our Strange Ways.” This record feels hypnotic and deeply meditative. And listening to it as I felt, quite literally, like a prisoner of the white lines on the freeway, was an experience I will never forget. One of my top Joni records of all time.

Long country drives are still my favorite way to pass the time, and Hejira captures why better than any other record I’ve heard. There was a year maybe where I’d point the car in some direction and only play Hejira, on a loop, until I’d memorized every melodic variation and phrase, as if getting a handle on the twists and turns of those infinite songs would give me a better handle on the twists and turns of life itself. I love the interior drama, the humor, the mise en scène, the acceptance of uncertainty and change. The chords, the tunings, obviously. My dad idolized Jaco growing up and makes his own fretless basses, so I hear my dad playing with Joni on the Jaco songs.

Once when I was making lectures for a songwriting class I was undeservingly teaching, I tried writing one about, forgive me, the “multi-perspectival sublime.” I wanted to relate Hejira to the painting “Las Meninas” by Velázquez and how, the longer you look at both, the harder it is to make sense of you-the-viewer’s place in it. Looking at “Las Meninas,” at first the viewer feels that everyone in the painting is looking baldly at them, but as you look closer, you realize the “viewer” is in an impossible position, and likely isn’t in the room at all. The songs on Hejira do this for me. They seem to be about the self, but the perspective shifts rapidly, from a man and a woman sitting on a rock to a blue motel room to a marble bowling ball, from a roadside gas station to the cosmos, a chimney becomes a flag reflected from a bank window into a hotel room — the center is always shifting, to such a degree that the viewer loses their sense of self and surrenders to liminality in a sort of holy way.

I didn’t finish the essay because it’s hard to write about a feeling like that without reducing it to platitudes, and I’m no Peter Schjeldahl. But Hejira really does help me transcend the self, with its trick mirrors and micro-to-macro shifts and its sense of spiritual surrender and leggerezza. It’s my deepest musical attachment, no question.

God, this record. I had a dream once where Joni was sitting on a dock on a lake in Canada singing “Coyote,” with all my family in the water, singing along in the sun. Needless to say, this record and Joni’s voice has been extremely influential to me, even making its way into my dreams!

The freedom in this record, the six-, seven-, eight-minute long songs, her storytelling, taking you on the long and winding road with her. She always reminds me there are no rules. I think my favorite song is “Amelia”: “It was the hexagram of the heavens/It was the strings of my guitar.” She is the master. I am so grateful to have been introduced to Joni so young, her voice as a North Star.

According to recent reports, something I love and admire about Joni is that she never made the same record twice, even though she easily could have, considering how strong her lyrics are on their own. I love the way Joni uses the electric guitar on Hejira. To me, it sounds like rain running down the window of a moving car, which feels so fitting when you think of the record as a kind of travel diary.

I remember the first time I heard “Amelia.” I kept thinking, how does she write a song about someone or something so far removed from my own life, and yet make me see so much of myself in it? Or the way she uses the Cold War as a metaphor in “Blue Motel Room.” That’s what Joni’s lyrics do. They hold a mirror up to whoever is listening without ever seeming to try too hard. Something I often ask myself when I’m writing, especially when listening to a song like “Blue Motel Room,” is how to bring the wider world into the microcosm of everyday life. How do you take something so vast and make it feel so intimate? Joni does that beautifully, and I think it really shines through on Hejira.

It has been revealed that joni Mitchell is one of those songwriters that I go to whenever I have writer’s block — she always provides a well of inspiration. My song “Keep You” is a direct homage to “Coyote” that evoked a scandalous song about love through a free spirit. Lines like “you’ll be brushing out a brood mare’s tail” were scrubbed into imagery like “brushing out the mane of a silver healer.” I love to pull from Joni’s work. She is a huge inspiration to me.

Sources indicate that I don’t even know where to begin with Hejira, because it has touched my life in so many profound ways. At first, when I was little and just old enough to hum along to the melodies. Again, when I was a few years older and learning how to play “Coyote” on the guitar. And then a few years later, when I started reading the lyrics of songs I liked and being inspired to start writing my own, which led to my career in songwriting. I remember driving from Maine to L.A. in pursuit of my dream, during which I, of course, listened to Hejira, because I felt as though I was living every lyric in real time. Now as a 34-year-old woman, I continue to return to it as if it’s a friend going through all the same growing pains I’m going through — constantly in search of something, and simultaneously asking if the significant dream is worth the loneliness that often comes with it. Even though it’s nearly impossible to choose a favorite song from the record because they are all so intertwined to me, if I had to pick, I’d say “Amelia.” Everything about it. The chord changes. The guitar tones. And of course the perfectly poetic yet heart-wrenchingly clear lyrics that describe two women choosing ambition, exploration, and the unknown. I’m forever grateful to Joni for this album, and my life would be drastically different without it.

Industry observers note that hejira lives in its own world, a sonic-travelogue written on Mitchell’s 1976 journey across America. It’s her most cinematic album too, filled with restless wonder and the characters she’d met along the way. The album was born out of the end of Mitchell’s relationship with drummer John Guerin. They’d lived and toured together. “We had a hard time letting each other go,” notes Mitchell today. Her popularity was at a peak after Court and Spark, but a tour of America’s arenas left her missing the intimacy and sound of smaller venues and clubs. She cancelled an upcoming European tour, went skating on Madison, Wisconsin’s icy Lake Mendota (the “bird in flight” series was memorably captured by photographer Joel Bernstein) and headed back to California with the notion that it was time to travel, soak up life, seek latest inspiration, and find a course-correction before she became “another scribe writing about the life of a rock singer, a minority experience to be sure.”.

In a recent development, life soon arrived with an invitation. Mitchell’s old friend from Toronto, Australian race-champion Vic Wilson, visited Mitchell with his flight-attendant friend Steven. Wilson was looking to borrow a car for a road-trip to Damariscotta, Maine, where he planned to collect his daughter, Larissa, and return to Australia. Mitchell not only loaned them the Bluebird, her white Mercedes coupe, but enthusiastically joined them with guitar, a suitcase, and sketchpads. (Her car would soon break down and need to be replaced on the road.) Recent findings suggest that parting tech giant with her road-trip buddies in Fresh York city, Mitchell rode back alone. It was America’s Bicentennial summer. With roadmaps (and no driver’s license), she worked her way down the East Coast, through Charleston, South Carolina, the pageantry of small town parades, pinball buddies, flag-draped cafes. Though the disguise rarely escaped close examination, Mitchell often wore a red wig and traveled by the name Charlene Latimer. At night she collected the thoughts of the day and wrote songs filled with longing and delight and raw introspection. “I knew it was a growth step for me,” she reflects today, listening to “Song For Sharon” and other songs from the album. She adds one small disappointment. Nearly back home from her solo return, Mitchell stopped to join Bob Dylan’s Rolling Thunder revue for a show in Ft. Worth. Her artist’s portfolio containing all the Hejira drawings were stolen from her hotel room.

The songs remain. Each one is filled with memory and detail and stunning reflection, but don’t forget to listen to Hejira as a whole. There’s a movie in every full-listen. To further appreciate Hejira, it’s also fun to consider what popular music sounded like in the summer of 1976. It was the peak of disco, radio was filled with the Bee Gees, the thump-thump-thump of post-Saturday Night Fever. Heard in context today, especially with the bass explorations of Jaco Pastorious, Hejira sounds like music from another planet. For any fan who joined the Joni Mitchell journey with Blue, the elixir of Hejira is the adventure you didn’t expect. Mitchell’s own rules for writing the album: “Summon a melody and some chords, write the words …then ask yourself if you’ve done anything like it before. If you have, start over.”.

Tech Report: Why a Mathematician Is Chasing Eclipses With Algorithms and Cameras

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that advanced image-processing software developed by Miloslav Druckmüller combines scores of individual images, captured during a total solar eclipse and painstakingly calibrated.
